text:
oliver: Hi team — opened my first PR for the session-store refactor (branch feat/session/refactor). Quick orientation: should I squash my iterative commits before marking ready, and what's the minimal PR body folks expect?

sophia: Welcome! :wave: For a clean main we prefer squashed logical commits on merge. While iterating keep commits; before finalizing squash or rebase so the merge is a single logical change.

jen: For PR body, short and structured works best. Top line: ticket (SESS-12) + 1-line summary. Then three small sections: What, How to test, Rollback. Example: "What: move session serialization to new store; How: run `make dev` and POST /login; Rollback: revert config flag"

oliver: Thanks — pre-commit flagged import order and a type hint. Any way to avoid noise for reviewers?

sophia: Put formatting fixes in their own commit like `chore(format): apply isort/black`. Call out in the PR body "formatting only commit" so reviewers can skip it.

jen: CI checks we watch: ci/lint, ci/unit, ci/typecheck. If unit tests fail only on CI and pass locally try re-running the job or add `ci-flake` label.

code-bot: Tip: comment `@code-bot request-review` after you mark ready to auto-assign CODEOWNERS.

oliver: One more: what's the etiquette for force-pushes after reviewers requested? I had to rebase to resolve a conflict with main.

sophia: Use `--force-with-lease`; if you rewrite while reviews are active add a comment summarizing the changes and re-request review. Small fixes are fine, big rewrites should wait until reviewers sign off.

jen: If your change touches infra or public API, add `needs-approval` label and mention @infra-team or product. Otherwise reviewers usually give LGTM within a day.

oliver: Great — I'll split formatting into a separate commit, add the testing steps, run pre-commit, and request review. Appreciate it! :pray:
